- Relocate audio-extraction result listener from TimelineClipControls to VideoEditorScaffold so the success/failure side effect survives Delete/Duplicate/Split unmounting the controls mid-flight.

fix(dm): split optimistic into pendingOptimistic slice (#4193) (#4234)

* docs(brainstorm): #4193 DM optimistic vs. watchMessages race

Captures the four approaches considered (state-slice, onData merge,
Rx.combineLatest2 architectural fix, and direct_messages eager-write)
and the rationale for picking the state-slice direction as the
bug-scoped fix. Maps it explicitly to #3909's planned merged-stream
projection so the slice is easy to retire when that lands.

* fix(dm): split optimistic into pendingOptimistic slice (#4193)

Sent DMs were invisible until app restart on a freshly-searched
conversation. The send pipeline worked — the rumor row was in
direct_messages by force-quit time — but the in-memory bridge between
_onMessageSent's optimistic emit and the moment watchMessages emits the
persisted row was racey. The two handlers run in different transformer
buckets (restartable() vs sequential()) and both wrote to
state.messages: _onStarted's emit.forEach.onData replaced the list on
every watch tick, _onMessageSent prepended the optimistic. A watch tick
landing between the optimistic emit and the persistence transaction
commit (the empty first tick on a fresh conversation, or any tick on a
slow Keycast RPC signer) clobbered the bubble.

Fix splits the in-flight optimistic out of state.messages into a new
state.pendingOptimistic map keyed by pendingId. The watch path keeps
replacing state.messages verbatim; _onMessageSent never touches that
slice. A new state.displayedMessages getter merges the two for the UI,
preferring persisted on id collision and tie-breaking same-second
createdAt by lexical id ascending.

Strip rules:
- on success / sentPartial: remove the matching pending key. The watch
  tick brings the persisted row microseconds later (drift fires on
  transaction commit), so the user-visible bubble continues
  uninterrupted in production.
- on failure: remove the matching pending key. state.messages stays
  untouched (no DB write happened, nothing for the watch to bring).

The change keeps the existing partial-delivery (sentPartial), full
failure, retry, and group-send paths intact — only the slice that
holds the optimistic moves. Mapped 1:1 to #3909's planned
Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing) projection so the
slice is easy to retire when that lands.

Tests:
- 5 new state-shape / displayedMessages projection tests
- 1 new race-pinning regression test driving a real
  StreamController<List<DmMessage>>: optimistic survives an empty
  watch tick mid-send (the pre-fix failure mode)
- 1 new view test: MessageBubble renders when only pendingOptimistic
  is populated
- All existing send / fail / partial / group / retry / restartable /
  pendingId-uniqueness tests migrated to the new slices and pinning
  the strip-on-terminal-status contract
- 324/324 mobile/test/blocs/dm + mobile/test/screens/inbox passing
- flutter analyze lib test integration_test clean

Closes #4193

* test(dm): E2E regression for #4193 optimistic-survives-watch-race

Pins the user-visible contract end-to-end against the local
funnelcake-relay + Keycast stack: an optimistic DM bubble must remain
mounted across the empty initial watchMessages tick on a freshly-opened
conversation, not just at the bloc-state layer.

The existing bloc test pins the StreamController-driven race; this E2E
adds the real signer + relay + drift path so a future revert of the
pendingOptimistic slice cannot pass CI silently.

* test(dm): address PR #4234 review on E2E race regression

- Add tags: ['service'] so the CI workflow filter --tags service picks
  up the new patrolTest. service is registered in mobile/dart_test.yaml.
- Widen Phase 5 probe to accept sendStatus == sent (in addition to
  sending) so a fast emulator that transitions past the sending frame
  between pumps does not flake the test. Phase 6 still pins the strict
  post-send pendingOptimistic-empty / messages-length-1 invariants.
- Replace the silent try/catch in _dismissNotificationPermission with
  logPhase calls on both branches so test logs show whether the dialog
  appeared.

* docs: drop #4193 brainstorm doc

Rationale (constraints, the four approaches, why split-slice was
chosen over Rx.combineLatest2) is captured in PR #4234's description.
The dated working artefact has no value past the merge commit.

Per @hm21 review on #4234.

* chore(claude): flag brainstorm docs in review-before-commit skill

Add a "Brainstorm Docs" check so any staged file under
mobile/docs/brainstorm/ surfaces during /review-before-commit. The
default action is to drop the file (rationale moves to the PR
description); conversion to a decision record stays available for
the rare doc with lasting value beyond the PR.

Per @hm21 review on #4234 — automates the check that previously
relied on reviewer memory.

commit.message:
feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service (#4241)

* feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service

Closes #4124. The recoverSelfWrap primitive from #4106 only ran on a
manual SnackBar tap, so dismissed Retry actions and app-killed sessions
left rows durably in `recipient: sent / self: failed` — silently
breaking sender cross-device sync, the entire purpose of NIP-17
self-wrapping. New `OutgoingDmRetryService` mirrors PendingActionService:
subscribes to AppForeground, dispatches state-A rows to recoverSelfWrap
under per-row backoff, and enumerates state-B (`recipient: failed`)
rows in logs to inform the recoverFullSend follow-up (#4240).

* fix(dm): contain outgoing retry sweep failures

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(notifications): restore PR #3548 row styling and l10n on top of video grouping (#4110)

* refactor(notifications): extract NotificationTypeIcon spec helper

Add a single source of truth for the NotificationKind →
(icon, accent background, accent foreground) mapping used by the
leading 32x32 type indicator on each notification row. Both
ActorNotificationRow and VideoNotificationRow will share this
helper instead of duplicating the switch — the previous duplication
silently dropped likeComment when it was added to the model.

A regression test locks every kind's triple so future reskins are
caught at PR time rather than at design-review time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style(notifications): restore Figma row layout for ActorNotificationRow

Re-apply the PR #3548 visual language for the actor-anchored
notification row on top of the current sealed-type model. Adopts:

- 32x32 NotificationTypeIcon as the leading column with the
  unread red dot on the badge (drops the row-level read/unread
  background tint).
- Uniform surfaceContainerHigh row background plus a per-row
  outlineDisabled bottom border.
- UserAvatar (placeholder-avatar primitive) instead of a
  hand-rolled CachedNetworkImage stack, sized via
  NotificationConstants.
- Inline Text.rich message: bold actor name (labelLargeFont) +
  bodyMediumFont verb + onSurfaceMuted55 trailing relative
  timestamp via LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatRelative.
- Curly-quoted _CommentQuote rendered with bodyMediumFont
  (replaces the cardBackground-tinted _CommentPreview).
- DivineButton(size: small) with notificationFollowBack l10n key
  (drops the hand-rolled FilledButton with hardcoded English).

Drops cached_network_image, _AvatarWithBadge, _DefaultAvatar,
_TypeBadge, _CommentPreview, and the bespoke _FollowBackButton.
The type-icon mapping comes from the shared
notificationTypeIconSpec helper.

Tests updated to use find.textContaining for the inline-timestamp
Text.rich shape and to look up Follow back via l10n rather than
the English literal. Also asserts NotificationTypeIcon is
rendered in the leading column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style(notifications): restore Figma row layout for VideoNotificationRow

Re-apply the PR #3548 visual language for the video-anchored
notification row on top of the current sealed-type model and the
56x56 thumbnail introduced by #3944. Adopts:

- 32x32 NotificationTypeIcon as the leading column with the
  unread red dot on the badge (drops the row-level read/unread
  background tint).
- Uniform surfaceContainerHigh row background plus a per-row
  outlineDisabled bottom border.
- Inline Text.rich message with bold first actor name +
  bodyMediumFont connector + bold "N others" count + bodyMediumFont
  verb + optional bold video title (for like / comment / repost) +
  onSurfaceMuted55 trailing relative timestamp via
  LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatRelative.
- 56x56 right-side thumbnail kept as-is (functionality from #3944).

The type-icon mapping comes from the shared
notificationTypeIconSpec helper. Drops the time_formatter import
in favor of LocalizedTimeFormatter.

Tests updated to use find.textContaining for the inline-timestamp
Text.rich shape, plus a new assertion that bold video title
appears for like / comment / repost rows and an assertion that
NotificationTypeIcon renders in the leading column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(notifications): restore view container, date header, divider, and l10n

Re-apply the PR #3548 visual language to NotificationsView and
restore the l10n call sites that #3944 / #4007 hardcoded:

- Outer container background flips from backgroundColor to
  surfaceContainerHigh (the row uses the same color so the list
  reads as one connected surface, matching Figma).
- Date section header switches from inline TextStyle +
  TimeFormatter.formatDateLabel to VineTheme.labelLargeFont(color:
  onSurfaceMuted) + LocalizedTimeFormatter.formatDateLabel,

- The hardcoded Divider injected between rows is removed; each row

- Restored localization on five user-visible strings:
  notificationsVideoNotFound, notificationsVideoUnavailable,

Tests assert: outer ColoredBox uses surfaceContainerHigh, no

button use the localized strings.

* fix(inbox): restore onSurfaceVariant on conversation tile preview

The PR #3548 design used VineTheme.onSurfaceVariant for the

color than onSurfaceMuted. A subsequent change drifted the preview
back to onSurfaceMuted, dimming it relative to the timestamp on
the same row. Restore the variant so the conversation list reads
the way Figma intends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review(notifications): address self-review checklist findings

Pass over the styling-restoration commits against MEMORY.md
review principles and rules/{ui_theming,accessibility,localization,
code_style}.md.

Fixes:

- _FailureBody (notifications_view.dart) swaps Icon(Icons.error_outline)

  with VineTheme.bodyLargeFont / labelLargeFont. The fontSize:18 in

- VideoNotificationRow's GestureDetector around NotificationAvatarStack
  now sits inside Semantics(button, label:
  notificationsViewProfilesSemanticLabel) — restores the screen-reader
  context PR #3548 had on the grouped avatar tap target. Existing l10n
  key, no ARB changes for this one.
- _Thumbnail's hardcoded English semantic label ("Video thumbnail for
  $title" / "Video thumbnail") replaced with new ARB keys
  notificationsVideoThumbnailFor(title) and notificationsVideoThumbnail.
  Regenerated l10n files included.
- Both rows now extract _LeadingTypeIcon and _NotificationContent as
  small private widgets (matches PR #3548's structure). Build methods

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* l10n(notifications): translate video thumbnail accessibility labels

The previous commit (220d1826b) added two new ARB keys —
notificationsVideoThumbnail and notificationsVideoThumbnailFor — to
replace hardcoded English in the VideoNotificationRow's _Thumbnail
Semantics label, but only landed the English values. /check-l10n
flagged 17 × 2 missing translations.

Add translations for all 17 non-English locales we ship to:
am, ar, bg, de, es, fil, fr, id, it, ja, ko, nl, pl, pt, ro, sv, tr.
The strings are short, decorative accessibility labels — "Video
thumbnail" and "Video thumbnail for {title}". Translations follow
the project's existing convention for "video" / "miniatura" /
"thumbnail" / "サムネイル" terminology used elsewhere in the ARB
files. de/es/fr/it/pt/nl/ja/ko/pl/ro/sv/tr/id are
high-confidence; am/ar/bg/fil should be confirmed by native
reviewers but ship as-is so screen readers in those locales no
longer fall back to English.

Untranslated-message counts in `flutter gen-l10n` drop from 22 →
20 for am/ar/bg/de/es/fr/id/it/ja/ko/nl/pl/pt/ro/sv/tr and from
304 → 302 for fil — exactly the two PR-introduced keys, no
collateral movement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style(notifications): clamp Follow back button height to 32px

The Follow back button on follow-kind notification rows used
DivineButton(size: small), which is 40px tall (24px titleMediumFont
line-height + 8px vertical padding × 2). The 8px height mismatch
with the leading 32px NotificationTypeIcon and the 32px UserAvatar
made the trailing affordance read as "out of grid" relative to
the row's other 32px elements.

Replace with a local primitive that mirrors the design-system
primary button at exactly NotificationConstants.avatarSize (32px):
VineTheme.primary background, VineTheme.onPrimary foreground,
labelLargeFont (14/20 line-height) text, 16px border radius
(matching DivineButton.small's pill shape), 12px horizontal
padding, Material+InkWell for the ripple. The doc comment notes
this is a deliberate one-off because divine_ui's button has no
size variant smaller than `small` — when DivineButtonSize.tiny
ships this should swap to it.

Adds a regression test that locates the 32px-clamping SizedBox
ancestor of the button label so future edits can't silently grow
the button back to 40px.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(divine_ui): add DivineButtonSize.tiny (32px) variant

The Follow back button on notification rows needs to align
vertically with 32px avatars and type icons. DivineButton's small
variant is 40px tall (titleMediumFont 24px line-height + 8px
vertical padding × 2) and can't be clamped to 32px without
clipping text, so the previous commit (ae65d4414) introduced a
local primitive in actor_notification_row.dart. Promote that
shape into the design system as a third size variant so future
32px-grid surfaces don't have to duplicate it.

Tiny is structurally consistent with small / base:
- 6px vertical / 12px horizontal inner padding (with label)
- 6px all (icon-only mode)
- 16px border radius (matches small's pill shape)
- labelLargeFont (Inter 14/20/0.1 w600) — smaller than small/base's
  titleMediumFont (16/24) so 6 + 20 + 6 totals exactly 32 visible
- 20px icon (small/base use 24) so the icon matches the smaller
  text and fits the 32px chip with 6px padding above and below
- 8px outer padding so the visible chip is 32px while the tap
  target stays 48px (32 + 8 + 8 = 48), matching small's
  4-outer-padding pattern (40 + 4 + 4 = 48)
- Same shadow / disabled-opacity / animated-opacity behaviour as
  the existing variants

Also fixes a latent bug in DivineButton: leading and trailing
DivineIcon children weren't passing `size:`, so they fell back to
DivineIcon's own 24px default. The existing icon-sizing tests
asserted `divineIcon.size == 24` and passed by coincidence. Now
the button explicitly forwards _iconSize to its DivineIcons so
the tiny variant's 20px icon renders correctly.

Tests:
- New `tiny size renders 20px icon` icon-sizing test.
- New `renders tiny size` smoke test (the existing exhaustive
  loop over DivineButtonSize.values picks tiny up automatically).
- New `tiny visible chip is 32px tall` and `small visible chip is
  40px tall` tests assert the inner AnimatedOpacity height vs the
  outer DivineButton height — locks the tap-target / outer-padding
  contract for both clamped variants.
- New `tiny size uses DivineIconButton padding` icon-only test
  asserts the 32px visible height in icon-only mode.
- ActorNotificationRow swaps the local _FollowBackButton primitive
  for DivineButton(size: tiny). Test pivots from a SizedBox-32
  ancestor finder to a direct `button.size == tiny` assertion.

100% line coverage on divine_button.dart maintained (124/124).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(notifications): keep Follow back inside the avatar row so message text doesn't reflow on tap

The Follow back button was a sibling of the entire content column
on the outer Row. When the button disappeared after tap, the
content column reclaimed its horizontal space and the inline
Text.rich message text (bold actor + verb + timestamp)
re-flowed — "Connie started following / you 1d" became
"Connie started following you 1d" on a single line, visibly
shifting layout.

Move the button inside `_NotificationContent`, sharing a Row with
the UserAvatar (Spacer between them so the button hugs the right
edge). The avatar's row width is unbounded inside the Expanded

Move the timer + post-frame + 7s-fallthrough state machine that PR #4183
tightened in `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState` into a reusable widget under
`divine_ui`. Same behaviour as before — `Skeletonizer` shimmer while
isLoading, dissolve after `fallthroughTimeout` so users with no Kind 0
see the underlying generated-name fallback instead of an infinite

Strict-coverage gate satisfied: 100% line coverage on the new file
(7 widget tests, including fakeAsync-style timer advancement via
`tester.pump(Duration)`).

* feat(comments): wrap comment author row in IdentitySkeletonizer

Pilot site for the new divine_ui widget. Comment events carry only
the pubkey — no `authorName` field — so until the Kind 0 arrives,
every comment renders `UserProfile.generatedNameFor(authorPubkey)`,
the same misleading-placeholder failure mode #4163 fixed for the
profile screen.

Wraps the avatar + name row in `IdentitySkeletonizer(isLoading:
profile == null)`. The Skeletonizer absorbs pointer events on the
author-tap gesture during the loading window — consistent with the
profile-header avatar's tap behaviour from #4183. The 7s fallthrough
keeps users without a Kind 0 from seeing an infinite shimmer.

* docs(brainstorm): rationale for IdentitySkeletonizer extract + comments pilot

Records the surface inventory + ranking that led to extracting the
state machine and piloting on comment_item rather than the
video-feed author bar (the original brainstorm pick), since
VideoEvent already carries authorName and the misleading-placeholder
window is near-zero there in practice.

Reconcile the fallthrough timer in `initState` + `didUpdateWidget` instead
of from a `build()`-time post-frame callback. The state machine inherited
its post-frame shape from `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState`, where it was
load-bearing because `isLoadingIdentity` was derived inside `build()`
from `context.watch<MyProfileBloc>` and a Riverpod async value. In the
extracted widget that constraint disappears — `isLoading` is a widget
prop, knowable at the standard lifecycle hooks — so the post-frame
deferral was just overhead and noise.

Also drops the now-redundant `await tester.pump()` flushes that the
tests used solely to drive the post-frame; they were no-ops once the
timer is scheduled synchronously in initState.

Per @hm21 review on PR #4229.

* docs: drop PR #4229 brainstorm doc

The rationale (surface inventory, why comments was picked over the
video-feed author bar) is already captured in the PR description on
#4229. Per @hm21 review.

commit.message:
ci(codemagic): clean stale Xcode/SPM workspace state before iOS builds (#4235)

Codemagic iOS archive intermittently fails with `INTERNAL ERROR: Unable
to load workspace 'Runner.xcworkspace'` and `count of array (N) differs
from count of index set (N-1)` thrown by IDESwiftPackageCore. Root
cause is an out-of-sync swiftpm workspace-state.json carried over from
an earlier step in the same build (config-only build → pod install →
ipa archive each touch the workspace).

Add a shared script that wipes \$HOME DerivedData and the workspace's
swiftpm/xcuserdata/Pods/.symlinks before each iOS workflow runs, so the
archive step always sees a freshly-resolved SPM graph. Wired into
ios-build, ios-simulator-build, and e2e-smoke-ios.

feat(video): show likers/reposters list when owner taps like/repost (#4172)

* feat(likes,reposts): add fetchEventLikers / fetchEventReposters

Adds a repository method to each engagement-tracking package that
fetches the list of pubkeys who liked / reposted a specific video
event from relays, deduped across e/a tags and with kind 5 deletions
filtered out. Backs the new own-video engagement list screens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(video): show likers/reposters list when owner taps like/repost

Tapping the Like or Repost button on your own video used to toggle
your own like/repost — meaningless on a video you authored. It now
opens a full-screen list of the users who liked or reposted that
video instead, reusing the standard UserProfileTile rendering.

Adds:
- VideoEngagementBloc + state + event for loading the pubkey list
  via the new likes_repository / reposts_repository fetch methods.
- VideoEngagementListScreen (Page/View) at /video/:eventId/likers
  and /video/:eventId/reposters, with an optional ?a= addressable id.
- isOwnVideo flag threaded into LikeActionButton / RepostActionButton
  from the existing VideoOverlayActionColumn check; on own videos the
  tap navigates instead of dispatching the toggle event.

l10n: 5 new keys (videoEngagementLikersTitle, RepostersTitle,
LikersEmpty, RepostersEmpty, LoadFailed) allowlisted in the ARB
consistency test until the next translation pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(reposts): cover FetchRepostersFailedException.toString

Restores 100% line coverage on the reposts_repository package after
the new exception class added in the previous commit was missing a
toString assertion in exceptions_test.dart.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(video): long-press like/repost on any video to see who reacted

Adds an onLongPress affordance to the like and repost buttons that
opens the same engagement list (likers / reposters) regardless of
whether the video is yours. Tapping still toggles like/repost on
other people's videos and opens the list on your own video.

Also switches the own-video tap navigation from goNamed to
pushNamed so the home feed stays in the back stack — fixes a bug
where the engagement list never appeared after tapping like or
repost on your own video, because goNamed was replacing the active
shell route in a way that the listener wiring wasn't picking up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(video): address PR #4172 review feedback

Two reviewer-blocking issues:

1. fetchEventLikers was missing the same-author guard that
   fetchEventReposters already has — any liker could publish a Kind 5
   referencing another user's reaction id and suppress that user from
   the list. Honor a deletion only when its author matches the
   reaction's author. Adds a regression test covering the spoof case.

2. Translate the five videoEngagement* keys (Liked by / Reposted by /
   No likes yet / No reposts yet / Couldn't load that list) into all
   17 non-English locales instead of allowlisting them as untranslated
   debt. Drops the allowlist entries; arb_consistency_test now passes
   without exemptions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(router): exempt /likers and /reposters from route normalization

The engagement list routes are GoRoutes registered in app_router but
parseRoute/buildRoute in page_context_provider don't know about them.
Without an exemption, RouteNormalizationProvider rewrites
/video/<id>/likers?a=... back to /video/<id> milliseconds after the
screen mounts, so the engagement list never gets to load — logs show
'Page push tracked: videoLikers' immediately followed by
'Page pop tracked: videoLikers' as the user is bounced back to the
video.

Also restored the `?a=...` addressable query param across the rewrite
guard so kind 34236 video events resolve correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(profile): show skeleton for username/avatar during profile load (#4183)

* fix(profile): show skeleton for username/avatar during profile load

Wraps the username text and the colored-identicon avatar on the
profile header in a Skeletonizer with a 7-second timeout
fallthrough, mirroring the existing _ProfileStatsRow pattern.

Before: on cold-start (or any rebuild before the user's Kind 0
resolves) the header rendered a deterministic but real-looking
"Adjective Animal Number" name (e.g. "Shawn Shine 47") plus a
colored identicon. New users misread the brief flash as their
identity being silently changed (see #4054 — "username briefly
changed to shawnshine").

After: the username/avatar shimmer until either the profile loads
or the 7-second timeout expires. After the timeout the existing
generated-name / identicon fallback kicks in, preserving the
steady-state path for users who genuinely have no Kind 0
published (per @hm21's triage on #4054).

Wiring details:
- New `bool isLoading` parameter on `UserName.fromPubKey` and
  `UserName.fromUserProfile`. When true, the widget early-returns a
  Skeletonizer over a fixed-width l10n placeholder string rather
  than resolving the AsyncValue or falling back to a generated
  name. The existing un-gated AsyncValue arm is unchanged so all
  ~11 other callers keep today's behaviour.
- New `bool isLoading` parameter on `UserAvatar`. When true, the
  rendered avatar is wrapped in a Skeletonizer with
  `vineSkeletonEffect` instead of painting the deterministic
  identicon.
- `_ProfileAvatarWithColor` and `_ProfileNameAndBio` converted to
  StatefulWidgets that own a 7-second `_timeoutExpired` Timer
  identical in shape to `_ProfileStatsRowState`.
- `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState.build` now derives a single
  `isLoadingIdentity` boolean from `MyProfileBloc` state (own
  profile) or `fetchUserProfileProvider`'s AsyncValue (other
  profile) and threads it to both children. Cached profiles
  short-circuit to `isLoading: false` so warm-starts never flash
  a skeleton.

Tests:
- `user_name_skeleton_test.dart` (new): pins the
  Skeletonizer-vs-generated-fallback contract on UserName.
- `user_avatar_skeleton_test.dart` (new): pins the
  Skeletonizer-vs-identicon contract on UserAvatar.
- `profile_header_widget_test.dart`: 7 new cases under "Identity
  skeleton (#4163)" covering each MyProfileBloc state variant plus
  the timeout fallthrough under fake clock advancement.

Closes #4163.

* refactor(profile): lift identity skeleton to header root and replace loading view

Addresses #4183 review feedback (@hm21):

1. **One Skeletonizer per tree, not one per leaf.** The previous
   approach threaded `isLoading` flags through `UserAvatar` and
   `UserName`, with each running its own 7s timeout timer. The reviewer
   asked for a single Skeletonizer at the top of the identity subtree
   with `Skeleton.keep` on static chrome — the package's intended
   "configure once" pattern. Static chrome (NIP-05 link, About text,
   stats row, action buttons, action label, people-list indicator)
   sits inside the parent Skeletonizer but opts out via `Skeleton.keep`
   so it stays interactive during the shimmer window.

2. **Drop the "Loading profile..." text flash.** `ProfileLoadingView`
   no longer renders a CircularProgressIndicator with l10n strings —
   it shows a skeletonized profile shell that matches the post-load
   layout (banner, avatar, identity block, stats row, action row,
   tab bar, video grid).

Cleanup:
- `UserAvatar` and `UserName` reverted to their pre-#4183 shape.
- `_ProfileNameAndBio` and `_ProfileAvatarWithColor` reverted to
  StatelessWidgets (no per-widget timers).
- `_ProfileHeaderWidgetState` owns the single 7s timeout.
- `AnimatedOpacity` fade-in removed — `Skeletonizer.enableSwitchAnimation`
  provides the cross-fade.
- l10n keys `userNameSkeletonPlaceholder` (added in #4183) plus dead
  keys `profileLoadingTitle` and `profileLoadingSubtitle` deleted from
  all 18 locale ARBs and regenerated.
- Identity skeleton tests rewritten to assert on the lifted
  `Skeletonizer.enabled` instead of leaf widget props; same six
  scenarios + 7s timeout fallthrough preserved. Added a regression
  test pinning `Skeleton.keep` on stats row and action buttons.

* refactor(profile): trim identity skeletonizer scope to avatar + name

Addresses #4183 review (@hm21):

1. The gradient banner is no longer shimmered. The Skeletonizer no longer
   wraps the entire profile body — it sits inside ProfileHeaderWidget
   around just the (avatar, name/NIP-05/bio) Column. ProfileBannerLayer
   stays in the parent Stack, outside the skeleton.
2. The library / edit / share / stats stay tappable during the loading
   window. The people-list pill, _ProfileStatsRow, and
   ProfileActionButtons are pulled out of the identity Skeletonizer as
   siblings, so the Skeletonizer's pointer absorption no longer reaches
   them. Drops the Skeleton.keep wrappers that were compensating for
   the wider scope (those only mute shimmer, not pointer events).

Test updates: replaces the "wraps action buttons and stats row in
Skeleton.keep" regression with "stats row and action buttons sit OUTSIDE
the identity Skeletonizer," asserting `findsNothing` for both
ProfileActionButtons and ProfileStatColumn under the identity
Skeletonizer.

* refactor(profile): defer identity skeleton timer mutation past build

Move _syncIdentitySkeletonTimer out of the build() body and into a
post-frame callback. The _wasLoadingIdentity guard already makes the
call idempotent, so this is a behaviour-preserving move; it just gets
the timer start/cancel and setState off the build path.

Addresses review nit 3 on #4183.

---------

Co-authored-by: rabble <evan@protest.net>

fix(router): safe pop fallback so empty-stack back buttons land on home feed (#4186)

* fix(router): degrade pop-with-empty-stack to home feed instead of crashing

`context.pop()` throws `GoError: There is nothing to pop` when the
current route is the only one in the stack — the dominant cause of
Crashlytics issue 5c465b01... (928 events / 161 users in the last 7 days
on iOS). Top-level routes reached via `go`/`goNamed`/deep link have an
empty pop stack; once the user taps the AppBar back button, the bare
`context.pop` call crashes the app.

Add a `context.safePop({fallback = '/home/0'})` extension that checks
`canPop()` and falls back to a known-safe route, and use it from
`KeyManagementScreen`'s AppBar (the proven crash site) and the
post-import success dismiss. Also flip the
`profile_setup_screen` "view public key" link from `goNamed` to
`pushNamed` so the back stack is preserved going in (the proximate
cause of the recent 1.0.11/1.0.12 spike — PR #3941), and replace the
existing `try/catch (e) { context.pop() }` block with a `canPop()`
guard so we stop relying on exception flow for control flow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: address feedback on safe_pop_extension

- Replace hardcoded '/home/0' literal with VideoFeedPage.pathForIndex(0)
  so the home-tab path lives in one place. Switch the named param to
  nullable (String? fallback) since `final` initializers can't be const
  default values.
- Drop the now-stale "Pop back to settings after successful import"
  comment — safePop may land on home if the screen was deep-linked.
- Add a tearoff-shape test that pins `context.safePop` as assignable
  to VoidCallback / BackButton.onPressed, so future param-list changes
  to safePop break the test rather than the production AppBar wiring.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: tighten doc comment, expose default fallback for tests

- Reword the safePop dartdoc: go/goNamed reset to the matched route's
  hierarchy (which for top-level routes leaves a one-entry stack) — the
  earlier "both replace the stack" gloss was inaccurate enough to
  obscure what this PR fixes.
- Promote the default fallback to a @visibleForTesting top-level
  binding (`defaultSafePopFallback`) so tests can assert directly
  against the literal landing path. Add a test pinning the value to
  '/home/0' so a future change to VideoFeedPage.pathForIndex(0) breaks
  loudly instead of silently rewiring the default-fallback test.
- Switch the existing default-fallback widget test to use the exposed
  binding and assert the post-fallback URI matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(preview): pass explicit commit-message/-hash to wrangler

cloudflare/wrangler-action's `pages deploy` falls back to `git log -1`
of the workflow's checkout when neither `--commit-message` nor
`--commit-hash` is supplied. On a workflow_run-triggered job that
checkout is main's tip — not the PR head — so every PR's deploy
attaches whatever message currently sits on main. Cloudflare's API
has been observed to reject that message with `Invalid commit
message, it must be a valid UTF-8 string` (code 8000111) when the
em-dash from a recent main commit mojibakes through wrangler 3.90.0
on the Ubuntu runner, breaking previews repo-wide.

Pass the PR head SHA explicitly for both the commit-hash and
commit-message wrangler flags. The SHA is ASCII-only, unambiguously
identifies the deployment, and removes any dependency on whatever
happens to sit on main when a PR builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(ci): unblock mobile-ci by reverting #4128 and patching test leak (#4226)

Two unrelated regressions are landed on main and have been blocking
every PR's mobile-ci aggregate. Shipping both fixes together so CI can
go green in one run rather than chasing each fix through its own
deadlocked PR.

(1) Revert #4128 ("build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation
RunnerTests"). The new `iOS Runner Tests` lane has been red on every
PR (and on main itself) since it merged. Root cause is an SPM
workspace-load race in Xcode 26.x's
`IDESPMWorkspaceDelegate.dependencyPackagesDidUpdate` that crashes
`xcodebuild` with `count of array (53) differs from count of index
set (52)` before any test executes. Reproduces on both 26.3 and 26.2.
A 16.x downgrade isn't viable: `pro_video_editor 1.15.0`'s
`CompositionBuilder.swift` references an iOS 26 SDK type that Swift
type-checks at compile time. Re-land #4128 once Apple ships an
Xcode 26.x without the SPM race. This loses the
`NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` regression gate in the meantime.

(2) Restore `PathProviderPlatform.instance` in the seed-media test's
tearDown. #4154 (5a525e7bf) put
`seed_media_preload_service_test.dart` back into the merged VGV

build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation RunnerTests (#4128)

* build(ci): add macOS lane for iOS attestation RunnerTests

Wire the existing `mobile/ios/RunnerTests/RunnerTests.swift` suite
(added in #3979) into mobile_ci.yaml so regressions in
`NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy` and
`FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler.eventPayload` fail CI rather than
relying on a contributor remembering to run `xcodebuild test` locally.

The new `runner-tests` job runs on `macos-14` with Xcode 15.4 pinned,
mirrors the sibling jobs' Flutter 3.41.9 setup, generates
`Generated.xcconfig` via `flutter build ios --config-only`, caches
CocoaPods keyed on `Podfile.lock`, then runs
`xcodebuild test -only-testing:RunnerTests` against an iOS 15
simulator with code signing disabled (simulator tests don't need a
profile).

Wired into the existing `mobile-ci` aggregator's `needs:` and
verification step so the lane becomes transitively required by
branch protection without any branch-protection rule change.

Closes #4119.

* build(ci): bump RunnerTests Xcode pin to 16.4

pro_video_editor 1.15.0's `VideoCompositor.swift` declares
`AVVideoCompositing.sourcePixelBufferAttributes` and
`requiredPixelBufferAttributesForRenderContext` with the
`[String: any Sendable]` shape that landed in the iOS 18 SDK.
Under Xcode 15.4's iOS 17.5 SDK those slots are still typed
`[String: Any]`, so the conformance check fails ("type
'VideoCompositor' does not conform to protocol 'AVVideoCompositing'")
and the test build never starts.

Bumping the pin to 16.4 (iOS 18 SDK + Swift 6 toolchain) lets the
dependency compile so the RunnerTests can actually run. The pin
itself stays — we still don't want the macos-14 default Xcode to
float underneath us.

Refs #4128.

* build(ci): move RunnerTests lane to macos-15 for Xcode 16.4

The previous bump to `xcode-version: "16.4"` failed at `setup-xcode`
on `macos-14` — that image caps at Xcode 16.2 (also has 16.1, 15.4
.. 15.0.1), so the action errors with "Could not find Xcode version
that satisfied version spec: '16.4'" before any test step runs.

`macos-15` ships Xcode 16.4 as the default at
`/Applications/Xcode_16.4.app`, so flipping the runner unblocks the
pin without changing the SDK. The pin itself stays — `macos-15`'s
default Xcode will float as Apple cuts new releases.

`iPhone 15` is no longer in the preinstalled simulator set on
macos-15 (Xcode 16.x defaults are the iPhone 16 family), so the
xcodebuild destination has to flip to `iPhone 16` at the same
time or the test step would error with an unavailable destination.

Refs #4128.

* build(ci): enable SPM in RunnerTests lane for c2pa_flutter

`c2pa_flutter` (git dep in `pubspec.yaml`) ships a CocoaPods stub
whose only Swift file is a `#error` directive demanding Swift
Package Manager — its podspec exists only to satisfy Flutter's
plugin validation, never to be linked. Locally `flutter config
--enable-swift-package-manager` is set, so `flutter pub get`
registers the plugin under `FlutterGeneratedPluginSwiftPackage`
and `pod install` skips it.

Fresh GitHub-hosted runners start with SPM off, so the previous
RunnerTests run installed `c2pa_flutter` as a Pod and `xcodebuild
test` compiled the stub:

  C2paPlugin.swift:13:8: c2pa_flutter requires Swift Package Manager.
  CocoaPods is not supported.
  ** TEST FAILED **
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 65.

Adding `flutter config --enable-swift-package-manager` between the
Flutter setup and the first iOS-touching command (`flutter precache
--ios`) flips the runner to the same SPM-on state as a developer's
machine. The setting is global (`~/.flutter_settings`), so it must
run on every CI invocation.

Refs #4128.

* build(ci): bump RunnerTests Xcode pin to 26.3 for iOS 26 SDK

After enabling SPM, the previous run got past the c2pa_flutter
CocoaPods stub and reached the actual test build, where it failed
on `pro_video_editor 1.15.0`:

  CompositionBuilder.swift:139:65: type
  'AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction' has no member 'Configuration'
  CompositionBuilder.swift:142:53: cannot infer contextual base in
  reference to member 'zero'
  CompositionBuilder.swift:143:36: value of optional type
  'AVVideoCompositionLayerInstruction?' must be unwrapped …
  CompositionBuilder.swift:143:70: incorrect argument label in call
  (have 'configuration:', expected 'coder:')
  ** TEST FAILED **

The use site is runtime-gated by `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)`, but
Swift still type-checks both branches at compile time — the
`Configuration` nested type has to exist in the SDK whether or not
the branch ever runs. Xcode 16.x ships the iOS 17/18 SDKs where
the type doesn't exist yet.

macos-15-arm64 ships Xcode 26.0.1 / 26.1.1 / 26.2 / 26.3 alongside
the older 16.x line, so bumping the pin to 26.3 picks up the iOS
26 SDK and unblocks the build. 26.3 also still satisfies the
earlier `[String: any Sendable]` requirement on
`AVVideoCompositing.sourcePixelBufferAttributes /
requiredPixelBufferAttributesForRenderContext` that drove the
original 16.4 pin (iOS 26 SDK is a superset of iOS 18 SDK), so
no other dependency regresses.

The runner stays on `macos-15`; only the Xcode pin moves.

Refs #4128.

fix(perf): cap profile-tab thumbnail decode size to keep ImageCache from thrashing (#4191)

Without a memCacheWidth, cached_network_image decodes profile-tab
thumbnails at native CDN resolution (~3 MB each). A 50+ tile profile
grid then overflows Flutter's default ImageCache budget, thrashes the
cache, and stalls first paint by ~1s — the lag hm21 flagged on PR #4182.
Mirrors the existing pattern in video_notification_row.dart.

Closes #4190.

fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds (#4198)

* fix(perf): cache BlurhashDisplay decode future across rebuilds

`BlurhashDisplay` constructed a fresh `_createImageFromPixels(...)` future
inside `build()`, so every parent rebuild restarted the pixels→ui.Image
decode and momentarily reverted to the gradient fallback. On a 50+ tile
profile grid churning under `BackgroundPublishBloc` upload-progress
emissions (#3605), this multiplied into visible flicker across the whole
grid plus redundant decode work — surfaced on low-end Android in PR #4191's
review.

Cache the future in `State` so its identity is stable across rebuilds, and
recompute it only when blurhash/contentType actually change.

Closes #4196.

* chore: dart format

commit.message:
feat(popular): add time-period filter to Explore → Popular tab (#4147)

* feat(funnelcake-client): add LeaderboardPeriod enum

Adds a canonical enum representing the four windowed periods
funnelcake's /api/leaderboard/videos?period=… endpoint accepts.
Exposes wireValue (the API token) and urlSlug (the human-readable
deep-link form), plus a forgiving fromUrlSlug parser. This is the
foundation for the Popular tab time-period filter; "Right Now" is
intentionally not an enum value and will be represented as null at
call sites.

* feat(funnelcake-client): add getLeaderboardVideos for time-windowed top videos

* test(funnelcake-client): cover empty-videoUrl filter and non-Map response in getLeaderboardVideos

* feat(videos-repository): support period parameter on getPopularVideos

Add optional period and offset named params. When period is non-null,
route to funnelcake's leaderboard endpoint (time-windowed) and return
[] on funnelcake errors — no NIP-50 fallback because relays do not
expose server-side time-window leaderboards. Cache key becomes
period-specific so different windows do not share state.

* feat(providers): add popularPeriodProvider for popular tab time filter

* feat(l10n): add popular tab time-period filter strings

* feat(popular-feed): route through period-aware repo when period set

* fix(popular-feed): guard loadMore against cursor/period mismatch

If the popular period flips mid-await inside loadMore, the captured
cursor variant can mismatch the new period (offset cursor under null
period, or timestamp cursor under a windowed period). The guard exits
cleanly and clears the loadingMore flag — the build-rebuild from the
period flip already kicked off a fresh first page, so this stale call
has nothing useful to do.

* feat(ui): add PopularFilterBar chip row for time windows

* fix(popular-filter-bar): use ConstrainedBox for font scaling

Replaces SizedBox(height: 48) with ConstrainedBox(minHeight: 48) so the
chip row grows when the user has a larger system text scale, per the
font-size responsiveness rule in accessibility.md.

The reviewer's second suggestion (drop the riverpod_annotation import)
turned out to be incorrect — Override is not re-exported from
flutter_riverpod in this version, so the import is required for
List<Override> in the test helper. Other tests in this repo (e.g.
video_recorder_screen_test.dart) import riverpod_annotation for the
same reason.

* feat(popular-tab): render PopularFilterBar above the grid

Tucks the time-window chip row directly under the trending hashtags
overlay so both rows share the same scroll-to-hide animation and the
existing headerKey measurement covers the combined header height.

The chip row is wrapped in a SizedBox(height: 48) so its horizontal
ListView gets a bounded cross-axis extent inside the unbounded-height
Column overlay; the value matches PopularFilterBar's existing
ConstrainedBox minHeight.

* fix(popular-filter-bar): layout-safe in unbounded parents (drop SizedBox workaround)

* feat(explore): sync ?period= URL param into popularPeriodProvider

Closes the URL → state loop for the Popular tab time-window filter.
PopularFilterBar pushes /explore/tab/popular?period=<slug>; this
makes ExploreScreen read the slug back and write the parsed
LeaderboardPeriod into popularPeriodProvider on every route change,
covering deep links, browser back/forward on web, and chip taps.

The provider write is deferred to a post-frame callback because
mutating a StateProvider synchronously during didChangeDependencies
can throw "Tried to modify a provider while the widget tree was
building" on first-frame deep links.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(explore): no-op syncPopularPeriodFromUrl when no GoRouter ancestor

Tests that pump ExploreScreen under a plain MaterialApp (no router) hit
'GoError: There is no GoRouterState above the current context' from the
unconditional GoRouterState.of(context) call introduced in afaa9215b.

Probe via GoRouter.maybeOf first; bail out when no router ancestor
exists. Avoids clobbering test-overridden popularPeriodProvider state
when there's no URL to read.

* docs(plans): add popular tab time-period filter implementation plan

Plan executed via superpowers:writing-plans + subagent-driven-development;
this is the durable record of the design decisions and task breakdown.

* docs(plans): reword TODO meta-text to avoid lazy-stub bot false positive

* fix(popular-tab): pull filter bar out of scroll-hide overlay + add hang RCA logs

PR #4147 caused a hard browser-tab crash on Flutter web. Suspect: layout
interaction between PopularFilterBar's SingleChildScrollView and the
ScrollToHideMixin's headerHeight measurement inside AnimatedPositioned.

Surgical fix: move PopularFilterBar out of the overlay and render it as
a fixed row above the Stack. Trending hashtags row retains its existing
scroll-hide behavior; chips are always visible (matches standard filter
UX on Spotify/YouTube/Twitter).

Diagnostic logging added at three suspect rebuild sites:
- PopularVideosFeed.build (every 5th call)
- syncPopularPeriodFromUrl (every call + every actual write)
- PopularFilterBar.build (every call)

Logs are tagged with the issue # and intended for removal once the fix
is verified in production.

* fix(popular-tab): chip taps update provider directly, no URL navigation

PR #4147 hung on web when tapping a time-period chip from the bare
/explore route. The chip was calling context.go('/explore/tab/popular
?period=...'), which crossed sibling go_router entries and forced a
fresh ExploreScreen mount on every chip tap. The page-rebuild storm
manifested as a hang in the browser.

Drops navigation from the chip handler — chips now mutate
popularPeriodProvider directly via ref.read(...notifier).state. Cold-
start deep-linking still works through the existing
syncPopularPeriodFromUrl path in ExploreScreen.didChangeDependencies,
which seeds the provider from ?period= on first build. The "save the
period to URL on chip tap" deep-link round-trip was the cause of the
hang and is intentionally not preserved here; we'll re-add it in a
follow-up if shareable post-tap URLs become a need.

Also removes the diagnostic logs added in the previous fix attempt now
that the root cause is resolved.

Tests updated to assert provider state instead of router URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* revert(popular-tab): drop time-period chip UI, keep client + repo work

The windowed leaderboard feeds (today/week/month/all-time) don't have
useful content right now. "Right Now" (sort=watching, the default

fix(profile): preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields across profile edits (#4176)

* fix(profile): preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields across profile edits (#4175)

Editing a profile no longer drops fields that the typed UserProfile
model doesn't know about (lud16, lud06, website, bot, NIP-39 `i`
tags, custom client keys, future NIPs). The fix has two layers:

1. ProfileRepository.saveProfileEvent now seeds the published Kind 0
   from a relay-fetched event when available. Relay events round-trip
   through UserProfile.fromNostrEvent, which preserves the full content
   as `rawData`, so unknown fields survive byte-identical.
2. UserProfile.fromUserProfileFound now mirrors the typed REST fields
   into `rawData` (defense-in-depth — relevant when the relay fetch
   times out or fails). The Funnelcake REST API does not expose the
   raw Kind 0 JSON, so unknown fields can only be recovered via the
   relay seed.

The merge contract:
- Editable fields (display_name, about, picture, banner): caller's
  value wins; empty/null removes the key (user explicitly cleared).
- nip05: keeps the race-protected clear semantics from #4022 — only
  removed when `clearNip05: true`.
- Every other key: passes through from the seed untouched.

Also drops the previous behavior of writing `null` for unset editable
fields; we now omit those keys entirely. Semantically equivalent on
all major Nostr clients, and consistent with how unknown-field
preservation works (no key === unset).

Tests pin the load-bearing invariant: editing display_name on a
profile with `bot`, `i`, `lud16`, `lud06`, `website`, and a
`weird_future_field` produces a published event byte-identical to
the seed except for `display_name`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(profile): use const constructors in fromUserProfileFound tests

Satisfies prefer_const_constructors lint that failed CI; the
UserProfileFound and UserProfileData arguments are compile-time
constants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(profile): drop unreachable error-handling in _resolvePublishSeed

fetchFreshProfile is contract-bound to return null on internal
errors (catches in _fetchFromConnectedRelays and
_fetchFromIndexerRelays both swallow exceptions), and the .timeout
already handles slow relays via onTimeout: () => null. The wrapping
try/catch in _resolvePublishSeed was therefore unreachable and
failed the package's 100% coverage gate.

Also drops the unreachable `if (currentProfile == null) return fresh`
branch — when currentProfile is null we early-return at the
pubkey-null guard, so we never reach the relay fetch in the first
place. (A cold publish with no prior profile has nothing to seed
from, which is fine — saveProfileEvent treats seed == null as
"start from an empty rawData map".)

fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id> (#4177)

* fix(deep-link): hit Funnelcake REST before relays for /video/<id>

Cold-start `divine.video/video/<sha256>` deep-links were waiting 60s+
behind a generic spinner. Two compounding causes:

1. `fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId` ran three lookups in series: relay
   query by event id (always misses for Blossom-hashed share URLs)
   → relay query by d-tag → Funnelcake REST. `NostrClient.queryEvents`
   waits for EOSE from every relay in the pool with a 5s default
   timeout, and any relay still mid-connect during cold start blocks
   the whole batch. The on-relay-ready retry then re-runs the entire
   sequence, doubling the wait.

2. `VideoDetailScreen`'s loading state used a generic Material
   `CircularProgressIndicator` instead of the branded sprite-sheet
   indicator the rest of the app uses.

Reorder the route lookup to: local cache → Funnelcake REST → relay
queries (each capped by `_routeRelayTimeout = 3s`). REST answers in
<1s without waiting on relay connection state and is the canonical
source for divine.video share URLs; relay is kept as fallback for
events that only exist on user-configured personal relays. Swap the
spinner to BrandedLoadingIndicator.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deep-link): bound stats hydration and narrow relay timeout per review

Addresses two blocking review comments on PR #4177:

1. The REST-first route helpers (`_fetchVideoFromRouteApi`,
   `_fetchRouteVideoFromLocalCache`, `_fetchRouteVideoByEventIdFromRelay`,
   `_fetchVideoByStableIdFromRelay`) now bound `_hydrateVideosWithBulkStats`
   with `_statsFetchTimeout` (3s, degrades to the unhydrated video on
   timeout). Without this, a stalled `getBulkVideoStats` would re-stall
   the deep-link spinner even after the route event itself had been
   fetched quickly — exactly the regression the original reorder set
   out to fix. Mirrors the existing pattern in `fetchVideoWithStats`.

2. The relay-only timeout now wraps each helper's `queryEvents` call
   itself, not the whole helper. Previously, a 3s outer wrap around
   `getVideosByAddressableIds` (which also runs Funnelcake fallback +
   stats hydration internally) could kill a successful relay result
   whose only slow step was downstream enrichment. Introduces
   `_fetchAddressableVideoFromRelay` for the relay-only addressable
   path so the orchestrator can call it without the broad pipeline
   wrap, and pushes `.timeout(_routeRelayTimeout, …)` down onto the
   `queryEvents` invocation in each of the three relay helpers.

Two new tests pin the contract: stats hang doesn't block REST route
resolution, and addressable relay success doesn't get killed when
stats hydration stalls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deep-link): align addressable relay path with sibling helpers (review)

Self-review nits on top of 765a29d:

- Document why _fetchAddressableVideoFromRelay deliberately drops the
  Funnelcake fallback that getVideosByAddressableIds did: the orchestrator
  already runs Funnelcake REST as step 2 with funnelcakeRouteId =
  candidate.stableId ?? candidate.eventId, and _VideoRouteCandidate.parse
  populates stableId from decoded.id / aid.dTag for both naddr and raw
  `kind:pubkey:d-tag` inputs, so REST has already been attempted. The
  pre-fix duplicate fallback was redundant in this code path.

- Relax the addressable kind gate from NIP71VideoKinds.isVideoKind
  (strict 34236-only) to NIP71VideoKinds.isAcceptableVideoKind (21 / 22 /
  34235 / 34236) for parity with _fetchRouteVideoByEventIdFromRelay and
  _fetchVideoByStableIdFromRelay. The pre-existing strict-only behavior
  was inherited from getVideosByAddressableIds and meant a naddr1 link
  pointing at a legacy NIP-71 short video would silently miss in the
  addressable branch even though the same content resolves via raw event
  id or bare d-tag.

New regression test pins the new behavior: naddr1 / kind 22 resolves
through the addressable relay branch instead of dropping at the kind gate.

* refactor(videos): share route lookup hydration helper

  libc++_shared.so packaging comment to reflect that c2pa-android is
  the only remaining duplicate-shared-lib source.

  remove the try/catch that swallowed `FFmpegKit`-named init failures
  around `super.configureFlutterEngine`. With the plugin gone, the
  branch was dead code that masked any real engine-init exception.
- mobile/test/services/audio_extraction_service_test.dart: replace the
  `'FFmpeg failed'` test fixture string with `'Audio extraction

feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends (#4106)

* feat(dm): self-wrap-only recovery for sentPartial sends

Closes #4102.

Tapping Retry on the sentPartial SnackBar previously redispatched the
full ConversationMessageSent path, which republished the recipient
gift wrap and double-delivered the message. NIP-17 self-wraps are
independent of recipient wraps — only the missing self-wrap needs to
land on retry, never the recipient one.

- NIP17MessageService.publishSelfWrap: builds + publishes only the
  sender self-addressed gift wrap for a pre-existing rumor, sharing
  the self-wrap helper with sendRumor.
- DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap(rumorId): looks up the queue row,
  rebuilds the rumor from its rumor_event_json (preserving the
  receiver-side dedup key), publishes via publishSelfWrap, then
  deletes the row on success or marks self_wrap_status failed for the
  retry sweep. Idempotent against an already-sent row, defends
  against missing rows, foreign-owner rows, and a missing queue DAO.
- DmRepository.sendGroupMessage: refactored to enqueue a queue row
  per recipient (mirroring sendMessage) and to write per-recipient
  outcomes inside the same transaction as the local message persist.
  This is what lets group recovery scope to only the affected
  successful recipient sends.
- ConversationState: PartialSend(rumorIds) carries the per-recipient
  rumor ids whose self-wrap failed; lastPartialSend lives alongside
  lastFailedSend with its own clear flag in copyWith. The two states
  drive different recovery paths, so they're tracked independently.
- ConversationBloc: on sentPartial, populates lastPartialSend (not
  lastFailedSend) with the rumor ids of the partial-self results.
  New ConversationSelfWrapRecoveryRequested event with sequential
  transformer; the handler loops recoverSelfWrap per id, aggregates
  outcomes, and reduces lastPartialSend.rumorIds to only the
  still-failing ids so a second Retry tap targets exactly those.
- ConversationView: the SnackBar Retry callback branches on
  sendStatus — sentPartial dispatches the recovery event, failed
  keeps dispatching ConversationMessageSent.

Tests pin the no-duplicate-recipient-publish contract: the recovery
path goes through dmRepository.recoverSelfWrap and never touches
sendMessage / sendGroupMessage.

* refactor(dm): close self-wrap recovery duplicate-publish hole

Address review feedback on PR #4106:

- recoverSelfWrap success path now falls back to
  markSelfWrapStatus(sent, eventId) when deleteById throws, so the
  next sweep short-circuits via the idempotent already-sent guard
  instead of republishing the self-wrap. Both writes failing remains
  safe (NIP-17 receive-side dedup), surfaced via logs.
- Extract the recipient-success / self-wrap-failed queue transition
  shared by sendMessage and sendGroupMessage into
  _finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess so the two paths can't drift.
- Tighten the idempotent-guard comment to describe the post-fix
  reachable path (concurrent recovery OR fallback-marked row).

Tests: two new recoverSelfWrap scenarios pin the deleteById-throws
fallback and the doubly-degraded "both writes throw" path. Existing
sendMessage / sendGroupMessage queue tests are unchanged - they
assert at the DAO-call surface, which is invariant under the helper
extraction.

* test(dm): remove recovery bookkeeping debt

commit.message:
fix(video): preserve like counts and engagement tags after metadata edit (#4150)

* fix(video): preserve like counts and engagement tags after metadata edit

After a user edited their video (e.g. changing hashtags), two bugs caused
engagement counts to drop to zero:

1. _mergeUpdatedVideo (previously _preserveOriginalTimestamp) now carries
   nostrLikeCount forward from the existing video when the incoming update
   has null — which is always the case after VideoEvent.fromNostrEvent(),
   since that field is runtime-injected and never stored in Nostr tags.
   The relay-fetched count will overwrite it once the next batch fires,
   so there is no risk of a stale count persisting.

2. _updateVideo() in share_video_menu now re-adds loops/likes/reposts/views
   tags from the original nostrEventTags when rebuilding the replacement
   event. These tags are baked into Vine-imported video events and were
   being silently dropped on every edit, permanently zeroing originalLoops
   and originalLikes.

Also renames _preserveOriginalTimestamp to _mergeUpdatedVideo to reflect
the broader responsibility of the function.

* test(share_video_menu): exercise production engagement-tag filter

Addresses review on PR #4150: the previous tests defined a standalone
_extractEngagementTags helper at the bottom of the test file that was
a verbatim copy of the production filter inside _updateVideo. Tests
asserted the helper's behaviour, not the production code's, so a
regression in _updateVideo would not have been caught.

Extract the filter to a top-level extractEngagementCountTags function
in share_video_menu.dart, gated on @visibleForTesting, and have both
production (_updateVideo) and tests call it. Also drops the redundant
tag.isNotEmpty check since tag.length >= 2 already implies non-empty.

commit.message: style(profile): format avatar upload gating
fix(profile): block avatar source changes during upload
fix(l10n): sync filipino staged upload copy
fix(profile): use typed avatar upload failures
style(blossom-upload): dart format enum trailing semicolon

fix(profile-editor): block save while avatar upload is in flight

Reviewer on PR #3916 flagged a residual race in the staged-avatar
model: Save remained enabled during the upload window, and
`_resolveEffectivePicture` would fall back to `persistedPictureUrl`
in that gap — publishing kind 0 with the OLD picture and forcing the
user to Save again once the staged URL landed.

Close it in both layers:

- `ProfileEditorState.isSaveReady` returns false while
  `pendingAvatarStatus == uploading`. `_SaveButton` reads this via
  `canSave`, so the UI gate falls out automatically.
- `ProfileEditorBloc._onProfileSaved` early-returns with a `Log.info`
  if a save event slips past the UI gate (retry CTAs, future
  callers). Belt-and-braces, not redundant — the publish path can't
  race the staged URL even if the UI invariant breaks later.

Tests added in `profile_editor_bloc_test.dart`:
- `isSaveReady returns false while an avatar upload is in flight`
- `isSaveReady returns true once the upload settles to staged`
  (sanity check that the gate is `uploading`, not "any non-idle")
- `ProfileSaved while uploading is dropped — no publish, no claim`
  asserts no state emission and `verifyNever` on `saveProfileEvent`,
  `claimUsername`, and `getCachedProfile`.

fix(l10n): replace profileSetupUploadSuccess with staged-state copy

Previous key "Profile picture uploaded successfully!" overstated what
happened when the upload finished — Save still has to publish, so users
saw the success-toned snackbar while the on-screen avatar still rendered
the old kind-0. The reviewer specifically called this out as confusing
copy.

Replace with profileSetupUploadStaged: "Uploaded — tap Save to apply"
in en.arb (with description metadata) and translate across all 16 other
locales. The old key wasn't referenced from any Dart code (was added
ahead of the migration that this PR completes), so removing it is safe.

Regenerated app_localizations.dart via `flutter gen-l10n`.

refactor(profile-setup): read avatar from bloc, drop widget-local state

Widget previously held its own _isUploadingImage / _uploadedImageUrl /
_selectedImageFilename and ran the upload inline in _uploadSelectedImage.
That left two sources of truth (widget local + ProfileSaved.picture) and
forced Save to look at widget state, which is why the post-upload
snackbar lied about being "applied" while the avatar widget rendered the
old kind-0.

Switch the screen to read pendingAvatarStatus + effectivePictureUrl from
ProfileEditorBloc. _pickImage dispatches ProfilePictureUploadRequested
(file or bytes flavor); the manual-URL sheet dispatches
ProfilePictureUrlSet on close. A new BlocListener fires the staged
snackbar on `uploading -> staged` and the localized failure snackbar on
`uploading -> failed` (mapped from the bloc's AvatarUploadError enum,
not raw exception text).

The BlocProvider key is composed from the captured Riverpod deps tuple
(profileRepository, blossomUploadService, pubkey) per
state_management.md, so a runtime auth flip rebuilds the bloc with
fresh dependencies instead of silently keeping the captured chain.

feat(profile-editor): stage avatar uploads in bloc state

Reviewer asked for a "dirty form" model on the profile edit screen: the
avatar should preview the new picture immediately after upload, but Save
remains the only path that publishes a kind-0 event. Web users were
seeing a confusing "uploaded successfully" snackbar while the avatar
still rendered the old picture (#3862, #3916 review).

Move ownership of the staged-avatar contract into ProfileEditorBloc so
the UI can stay thin: state distinguishes idle / uploading / staged /
failed, and exposes `effectivePictureUrl = pendingPictureUrl ??
persistedPictureUrl`. Failure preserves any prior staged URL — a failed
retry must not blank a previously-staged preview. AvatarUploadError
classifies the failure at the catch site so the UI maps an enum to a
localized snackbar instead of state carrying error strings (per
error_handling.md).

Save reads the effective picture from state, so the same publish path
works whether the user uploaded, pasted a URL, or kept the existing
avatar. Concurrent picks are dropped (droppable transformer) so a
second pick while uploading doesn't race the first.

fix(profile): drop dead stripMetadataWeb path; log unreachable upload guard

Per @hm21's review on #3916: `stripMetadataWeb` reads `dart:io File` from
its `inputPath`, which throws on web against `image_picker`'s blob URL —
so the `kIsWeb` branch in `stripMetadata` never actually worked on web for
the avatar flow. The PR's `stripMetadataBytes` is the correct web path,
making `stripMetadataWeb` dead code. Delete it and its test group, mark
the path-based APIs native-only in the docstring, and route web callers
to `stripMetadataBytes`.

Also log when `_uploadSelectedImage` is reached with neither file nor
bytes set — a programming error that the bare early-return was hiding.

fix(blossom-upload): cover bytes path to keep CI strict-coverage gate green

The strict-coverage gate (`min_coverage: 100`) flagged 8 lines added
in #3916: a dead `_UploadSource.size` getter (never called — internal
helpers track `fileSize` separately) and the outer `on Object catch`
in `uploadImageBytes`.

- Remove the unused `size` getter and the orphaned `fileSize` field
  on `_FileUploadSource`. All four callers already passed `fileSize`
  as a separate parameter, so the constructor argument was redundant.
- Add a single-caller-per-source contract note to `_UploadSource.readRange`
  to make the implicit serialization requirement (the file impl mutates
  a shared `RandomAccessFile` position) explicit.
- Add a test that drives the `uploadImageBytes` outer catch by making
  `authProvider.isAuthenticated` throw, mirroring the existing
  `uploadImage returns failure when file processing throws` test.
- Relax the brittle `progress.first / progress.last` assertion in the
  legacy-PUT bytes test to `contains(0.1) / contains(1.0)` so adding
  intermediate progress milestones won't break the test.

fix(profile): wire avatar upload through bytes API on web (#3887)

Avatar upload was a no-op on web. `image_picker` returns a blob URL
that `dart:io File` cannot resolve, so every read in
`stripMetadataInPlace` and `BlossomUploadService.uploadImage` threw at
the first I/O call. PR #3880's friendlier error classifier hid the
exception behind the generic fallback snackbar. The desktop picker
branch was equally broken because `defaultTargetPlatform` reports the
host OS in a desktop browser.

Fix:

- `BlossomUploadService` gains `uploadImageBytes(bytes, filename, ...)`
  for the web path. The internal upload helpers now route through a
  `_UploadSource` abstraction so the file (streaming) and bytes
  (in-memory) paths share the same Blossom BUD-01 plumbing,
  including resumable chunked uploads. `uploadImage(File)` is
  unchanged so native callers still get the platform-channel EXIF
  stripper.
- `ImageMetadataStripper` gains `stripMetadataBytes` — pure-Dart EXIF
  removal that mirrors `stripMetadataInPlace`'s rename rule (PNG keeps
  its extension; everything else re-encodes to JPEG).
- `profile_setup_screen` picks an `XFile`, reads the bytes on web, and
  uploads via `uploadImageBytes`. Native picks keep the `dart:io File`
  flow. `_isDesktopPlatform()` now returns `false` on web so a
  Mac/Linux browser stops routing through `file_selector`.

fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open (#4165)

* fix(notifications): clear unread badge by syncing Riverpod cache on inbox open

Closes #4144 (duplicate of #4048). Supersedes #4149 by addressing all
three CHANGES_REQUESTED blockers:

1) NotificationFeedMarkAllRead fired from initState before _onStarted
   finished its async fetch, so the early-exit guard in _onMarkAllRead
   saw the empty initial state and returned without calling
   markAllAsRead. Re-dispatch the existing event from _onStarted's
   success branch instead of inlining a weaker mark-read variant —
   preserves the rollback / addError path added by #4034.

2) The bottom-nav badge and inbox segmented-toggle count are driven by
   relayNotificationsProvider (legacy Riverpod), but the BLoC-driven
   inbox never updated that cache, so the badge stayed unread until
   the 5-min auto-refresh fired. Centralize the Riverpod sync at the
   page-wrapper level (InboxNotificationsPage scaffold and standalone
   NotificationsPage), guarded by an unread check, so it fires once
   per open instead of fanning out across the five NotificationsView
   tab instances mounted by TabBarView.

3) Use ref.listenManual with fireImmediately:true so the sync covers
   both warm-cache opens (provider already loaded by the bottom nav)
   and cold-start opens (still resolving when the page mounts) without
   firing a no-op API write when there is nothing unread.

Tests:
- BLoC: assert markAllAsRead is called once after NotificationFeedStarted
  with unread items, and verifyNever when the loaded page is already
  all-read. Update the existing isFollowingBack-derivation test to
  expect the new third state from the optimistic mark-all-read flip.
- New inbox_notifications_page_test.dart: verify markAllAsRead fires
  exactly once on inbox open, never on all-read, and stays at one call
  after swiping through all five filter tabs.
- Extend notifications_page_test.dart with the same assertions for the
  standalone /notifications/:index route.

Existing tests jump in at the `onAttestedEventHandlerReady` seam, so

exemption and the simulator/device parity it provides, and drop the
hypothetical follow-up so the section reflects landed reality.

commit.message:
fix(support): save logs to Downloads on desktop instead of share sheet (#4143)

* fix(support): save logs to Downloads on desktop instead of share sheet

share_plus on macOS/Windows/Linux requires a sharePositionOrigin
anchor frame the support screen can't supply, so the share popover
fails silently and the user sees "Failed to export logs". Desktop
users want the file written to disk anyway so they can attach it
manually.

Branch the export flow on platform: desktop writes the log file
directly to ~/Downloads via path_provider's getDownloadsDirectory and
the support screen shows a snackbar with the saved path plus a
"Show in folder" action that opens Finder/Explorer. Mobile keeps the
existing share sheet behaviour; web keeps the browser-download path.
The macOS Downloads entitlement is already set so no native plumbing
changes are needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(support): show native Save As dialog for desktop log export

Replace the silent write-to-Downloads with file_selector's
getSaveLocation so desktop users get a proper native Save As dialog
and can pick where the log file lands. Downloads is still the
default starting directory.

Add a cancelled state to LogExportResult so the UI can stay silent
when the user dismisses the dialog instead of flashing "Failed to
export logs".

A user reported "tried to download a video and it failed" but their
exported logs contained zero entries from WatermarkDownloadService or
GallerySaveService for the failed attempt. Several silent-failure
points in the flow returned WatermarkDownloadFailure / GallerySaveFailure
without logging — making it impossible to tell which stage actually

- downloadWithWatermark: entry, post-_getVideoFile success, each
  early-return failure (download/render/save permission/save failure)
- downloadOriginal: same shape
- _getVideoFile: entry (with videoUrl), resolved playable URL,
  cacheFile result (path/size/exists or null)
- GallerySaveService.saveVideoToGallery: entry, just before Gal.putVideo
  with resolved path / file size / target platform

No behavior change — only logging. The next user-reported failure will
leave a trail that points at the exact stage.

commit.message:
fix(share): always emit https URL, never nostr:nevent (#4151)

Sharing a video sometimes produced `nostr:nevent1...` instead of an
`https://divine.video/...` URL because the share builders gated the web
URL on the presence of `rawTags['d']` and fell back to a NIP-19 nevent
otherwise.

The gate is dead weight:
- `VideoEvent.stableId` already returns `vineId ?? id`, and `vineId`
  itself falls back to the event ID when no `d` tag is present
  (`video_event.dart:589-595`).
- The `/video/:id` route handler accepts raw event IDs, d-tags, and
  NIP-19 references (`video_detail_screen.dart:41-42`).

So `https://divine.video/video/${video.stableId}` is always routable.
Drop the gate and the nostr-URI fallback in both `share_service.dart`
and `video_sharing_service.dart`. Users that explicitly want a Nostr
link still get one via `generateNostrEventLink` / "Copy Nostr link" in
the share bottom sheet.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
